* **MCU-target detector, TinyissimoYOLO** (https://github.com/ETH-PBL/TinyissimoYOLO, commit `19bea4bd1ea1e2c29a6ee6b14bd7494ce8c6ba25`), tinyissimo-v8 (scale b), 256x256, 839,392 parameters. No pretrained checkpoint is published upstream; this model was trained in the cloud container on CPU for 30 epochs (batch 64, SGD, VOC 2007 trainval, final-epoch weights, no validation-based checkpoint selection; wall time 2.0 h). The upstream recipe is a_train_export.py: 256x256, epochs=1000, batch=512, SGD, GPU. Its accuracy is therefore that of an UNDER-TRAINED model and must not be read as TinyissimoYOLO's attainable accuracy. INT8: ONNX Runtime static PTQ, QDQ, per-channel INT8 weights and INT8 activations of every Conv; decode tail float; 200 VOC07 train calibration images.
* TinyissimoYOLO FP32 on the R2 KITTI test frames (712 images, VOC person->person, VOC car->car): mAP50 0.121, mAP50:95 0.031 (EfficientDet-Lite0 INT8 on the same frames: see the table). It was not used as the simulator's stage-1 detector.
* **Host-reference detectors** (MediaPipe EfficientDet-Lite0/Lite2, SSD-MobileNetV2; Apache-2.0, COCO-trained, SHA-256 pinned) are NOT MCU-class. VOC results use the COCO->VOC class map without fine-tuning; KITTI results map Car->car and Pedestrian->person.
* MACs: conv/depthwise/FC multiply-accumulates from the TFLite graph (MediaPipe models) or thop (TinyissimoYOLO, PyTorch graph at 256x256).
* Host latency: shared 4-core cloud container CPU, 1 inference thread, with other jobs running concurrently for most rows; treat host latencies as indicative only. **No Portenta H7 latency has been measured for any model.**
